persona.name: Aditi Rao
persona.course: MSc Business Analytics, University of Exeter
persona.visa: Student visa ends January 2027. Planning to switch to the Graduate Route, then needs a sponsored Skilled Worker role.

evidence.title: Churn dashboard for a UK retail bank client
evidence.raw: I made Power BI dashboards for a bank client to see which customers are leaving.
evidence.uk_version: Built a Power BI churn dashboard for a UK high-street bank client, used weekly by 40 relationship managers and linked to a 6% fall in account closures over two quarters.
evidence.outcome: 6% fewer account closures in two quarters
evidence.context_note: Infosys is one of India's largest IT services firms with major UK banking clients, so this is direct UK financial services exposure.

evidence.title: Automated weekly reporting with Python
evidence.raw: I wrote Python scripts so the team didn't have to make Excel reports by hand every Monday.
evidence.uk_version: Automated a weekly Excel reporting pack in Python and SQL, saving the team 12 hours a week and removing manual copy-paste errors.
evidence.context_note: Hours saved per week is the kind of measurable result UK recruiters scan for first.

evidence.title: Trained three new analysts
evidence.raw: When new freshers joined I was the one who taught them SQL and our data.
evidence.uk_version: Onboarded and mentored three graduate analysts, writing the team's SQL starter guide still used for new joiners.
evidence.outcome: All three were working independently within six weeks
evidence.context_note: In India 'freshers' means graduate hires. UK employers say 'graduates' or 'new joiners'.

evidence.title: MSc dissertation: food bank demand forecasting
evidence.raw: My dissertation was forecasting how much food a Devon food bank needs each week.
evidence.uk_version: Forecast weekly demand for a Devon food bank network with time-series models (Prophet, SARIMA), cutting forecast error by 18% against their spreadsheet method.
evidence.context_note: A UK partner organisation counts as UK experience and gives you a UK referee.

evidence.title: Volunteer data clean-up for a local charity
evidence.raw: I help a charity in Exeter on Saturdays with their volunteer spreadsheet.
evidence.uk_version: Volunteer data analyst for an Exeter community charity: cleaned and deduplicated a 4,000-row volunteer database and built a simple rota dashboard.
evidence.outcome: Rota planning time cut from a day to an hour
evidence.context_note: UK employers value volunteering highly. Put it under Experience, not Hobbies.

evidence.title: University hackathon runner-up
evidence.raw: We came second in the uni hackathon with a bus delay predictor.
evidence.uk_version: Runner-up out of 22 teams at the University of Exeter hackathon, leading data work on a bus-delay prediction app.
evidence.context_note: Good evidence for teamwork and working under time pressure questions.

sample_transcript:
Coach: Hi, I'm your UK careers coach. Tell me a little about yourself, what are you studying and what did you do before?
User: I'm doing an MSc in Business Analytics at Exeter, I finish in September. Before that I worked three years at Infosys in Bangalore as a data analyst.
Coach: Great. What's one piece of work from Infosys you're proud of?
User: I built Power BI dashboards for a UK bank client to track customers who were closing accounts. Around forty relationship managers used it every week and closures dropped by about six percent.
Coach: That's a strong result. Anything you automated or improved?
User: Yes, I wrote Python scripts for our Monday reports. Before, two people spent a full day in Excel, so it saved maybe twelve hours a week.
Coach: And outside work?
User: I volunteer on Saturdays for a charity in Exeter, I cleaned their volunteer database and made a rota dashboard. Also my dissertation is forecasting food bank demand in Devon.
Coach: What roles are you aiming for, and what's your visa situation?
User: Data analyst or BI roles, maybe product analyst. My student visa ends in January so I'll go on the Graduate Route, but long term I need sponsorship.

uk_game.title: Graduate schemes recruit a year ahead
uk_game.body: Applications open in September and many close by December for a start the following September. Direct-entry analyst roles are posted all year and usually close within 2 to 3 weeks.

uk_game.title: Spring weeks are mostly for first-year undergraduates
uk_game.body: As an MSc student, spend that time on summer internships, graduate schemes and direct-entry roles instead.

uk_game.title: Check the sponsor register before you apply
uk_game.body: Only employers on the gov.uk register of licensed sponsors can sponsor a Skilled Worker visa. Many smaller firms will hire you on the Graduate Route but cannot sponsor later.

uk_game.title: UK CVs are two pages
uk_game.body: No photo, date of birth or marital status. Lead each bullet with an action and a number. A cover letter is read for 'why us', not a repeat of your CV.

uk_game.title: Referrals and speculative emails work
uk_game.body: A large share of UK roles are filled through referrals or are never advertised. A 15-minute chat with someone inside often beats ten online applications.

stories.title: Winning over a sceptical client team
stories.situation: Relationship managers at a UK bank client did not trust a new churn dashboard.
stories.task: Get the dashboard used weekly within a quarter.
stories.action: Ran three short sessions with the managers, rebuilt two views around their own account lists and added a one-page guide.
stories.result: 40 managers used it weekly and account closures fell 6% over two quarters.

stories.title: Automating the Monday reports
stories.situation: Two analysts lost every Monday to copying data into Excel reports.
stories.task: Remove the manual work without changing what managers received.
stories.action: Wrote Python and SQL scripts to build the same 15 reports and set up checks for missing data.
stories.result: Saved 12 hours a week and stopped copy-paste errors.

stories.title: Bringing new graduates up to speed
stories.situation: Three graduate hires joined during a busy release.
stories.task: Make them productive without slowing the team.
stories.action: Wrote a SQL starter guide and paired with each of them twice a week.
stories.result: All three worked independently within six weeks.

stories.title: Messy data from a charity partner
stories.situation: The food bank's records had gaps and changed format twice.
stories.task: Produce a usable weekly forecast for the dissertation.
stories.action: Rebuilt the history, agreed rules with the operations lead and compared several models.
stories.result: Forecast error was lower than their spreadsheet method.

stories.title: 24 hours at the hackathon
stories.situation: Our four-person team had one day to build a bus-delay predictor.
stories.task: I owned the data and model.
stories.action: Split work by hour, kept a shared checklist and cut features that would not be ready.

stories.title: A deadline that moved forward
stories.situation: A client moved a reporting deadline forward by a week.
stories.action: Prioritised with my manager and worked through the backlog.

playbook.title: Find 10 people at target employers
playbook.body: Use LinkedIn's alumni search for University of Exeter, filtered by your target companies and job titles.

playbook.title: Ask for advice, not a job
playbook.body: Request a 15-minute call to hear how they got into the role. Keep the message under 80 words.

playbook.title: Prepare three questions
playbook.body: What the team works on, what good looks like in the first six months, and what they wish they had known.

playbook.title: Thank them within 24 hours
playbook.body: Mention one thing you learned. Follow up once after two weeks if a role opens.

playbook.title: Ask who else to talk to
playbook.body: One warm introduction is worth more than ten cold messages.

playbook.title: Ask about a referral only when a role opens
playbook.body: By then they know you. Make it easy: send the job link and two lines on why you fit.

tone_norms: Say 'I led' or 'I built', not 'I single-handedly'. Confident but understated wins.
Use 'we' for team results and 'I' for your part. UK interviewers listen for your exact contribution.

Arrive 5 to 10 minutes early for in-person interviews, join video calls 2 minutes early.
Address people by first name unless told otherwise. 'Sir' and 'Madam' sound overly formal.
